A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SACTOR and retain the original benchmark evaluations. The main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across reorganization. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original translation success, cost, idiomaticity, and failure results on TransCoder-IR and CodeNet, plus AVL-tree and URL-parser case studies.

after.justification: v3 reports retained and revised benchmark results, new CRust-Bench and libogg evaluations, component ablations, temperature experiments, and test-coverage measurements.

M1.justification: v1 uses an LLM to generate idiomatic verification harnesses. v3 Section 4.3 and Appendix L introduce co-produced JSON interface specifications, rule-based harness generation, struct round-trip checks, and localized LLM completion of unsupported mappings. This substantially changes verification. Separately, v3 Section 4.1 rejects dependency cycles, while its retained Appendix B still describes grouping them; that behavior remains unresolved.

E1.justification: The two original 100-program suites remain. The AVL-tree and URL-parser case studies are removed and replaced by 50 CRust-Bench repository samples and libogg's 77 functions. This substantially expands the represented repository-level C programs and adds multimedia-container APIs with complex buffers and pointer manipulation.

E2.justification: The C2Rust, Crown, C2SaferRust, and VERT comparisons remain, including VERT's TransCoder-IR-only participation. Appendix J.2 newly evaluates direct GPT-4o translation with minimal and interface-preserving prompts on CRust-Bench and libogg. These introduce a substantive comparison against using an LLM without SACTOR's translation pipeline.

E3.justification: v3 Table 6 reports temperature zero for the original five models, replacing v1's mixed settings, and specifies a dated GPT-4o version. New protocols include GPT-5 evaluation, function-level scoring, conditional idiomatic evaluation, and ten-repair-attempt direct-translation baselines. Actual sampling changes are unclear: v3 Section 5.1 says random sampling, but Appendix F.1 retains selection of the longest TransCoder-IR programs.

E4.justification: v1 provides failure breakdowns and case studies but no component ablations. v3 Appendices J-K add feedback removal, direct translation, Crown removal, unsafe-prompt variants, and temperature sensitivity experiments. Appendix F audits test coverage, while Appendix M adds detailed repository and libogg failure analyses. These substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: v3 Section 6.3 newly reports up to three complete translation runs per real-world sample; v1 specifies translation retries without a comparable outer-run count. This is a limited addition to run reporting, not evidence of increased statistical replication. Aggregation across runs, random seeds, and between-run uncertainty estimates remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Reported GPT-4o idiomatic success changes from 78% to 80% on TransCoder-IR and from 84% to 79% on CodeNet, under revised reported settings. Llama results, costs, and failure counts also change. New results include CRust-Bench's 788/966 unidiomatic and 249/580 conditional idiomatic successes, libogg outcomes, and ablations. Some revised failure-chart values conflict with accompanying prose.

T1.justification: The task-ordering pseudocode and test-based soft-equivalence concept are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation. The SPEC schema and round-trip checks are procedural additions. Appendix J.3's information-theoretic interpretation is informal rather than a formal result.

C1.justification: The two-stage translation objective remains, but v3 redefines the verification contribution around co-produced specifications and synthesized harnesses. It drops v1's zero-shot characterization and adds explicit contribution claims about feedback benefits and temperature insensitivity. Its real-world claims distinguish full unidiomatic coverage from conditional, partial idiomatic coverage.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit limitations concerning test coverage, static-analysis precision, unsupported C features, harness stability, model dependence, and cost. New interpretations explain model-dependent feedback benefits and attribute Crown's contribution to otherwise unavailable ownership and pointer-shape information. The earlier AVL-specific generics/FFI discussion disappears with that case study.

D1.justification: Appendices B.1, L, and N add preprocessing and compile-flag instructions, supported SPEC mappings, converter checks, and concrete specification/fallback prompts. v3 also discloses baseline model and attempt settings. However, its configuration table removes v1's hosting-platform, H100, and explicit Q4 information. Reported code and dataset access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted references for RustBelt, long-context limitations, CRust-Bench, and libogg, and removes the introductory ChatGPT reference. The existing translation literature and its broad LLM-versus-static-method positioning remain, despite substantial rewriting of the related-work prose.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, related work, and methodology undergo extensive rewriting and consolidation. Failure and cost analyses move to Appendices H-I, illustrative material moves to appendices, and a dedicated limitations section is added. The title and author list also change. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the overview and success-rate plots, adds attempt breakdowns for both translation stages, merges failure displays, and places the lint plot beside the unsafe-code table. It removes the old case-study plot and adds translation examples, ablation and temperature plots, a SPEC diagram, and extensive new results and mapping tables.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens weaknesses in v1's empirical justification: Appendices J-K test previously unisolated design choices, Appendix F quantifies verification coverage, and Section 6.3 provides broader repository-level evidence. Detailed harness specifications and explicit coverage-dependent limitations also improve assessability. Sampling and dependency-cycle contradictions, along with stale result summaries, remain material weaknesses, but the added controls and transparent evaluation evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
